dossier.overview:
An `.rtpks` file is a **Resort Tile Pack Source**: a ZIP archive with stable **Resort tile IDs**, a **runtime mesh pack** (embedded `pokemon_resort.rpak`), editable palette tabs, smart paths, material animation, gameplay tags, and collision authoring rules. The **Operations Desk Map Editor** is now the main authoring surface. Existing Pokémon DS Map Studio exports remain valid as source packs, but new tiles and organization changes no longer require that application.

**RTPKS v2** (manifest `version: 2`) remains the compatibility container. v1 packs are rejected. The editor updates the `.rtpks` file and its sibling **`.rtpks.meta`** sidecar together, including a new source hash, so the pair cannot drift during an editor save. Overworld placement happens in `.owmap` files via `tilePackage` + `tileLayers` (see owmap-format).

Materials may use ordinary image frames or exact `materialMotion` (sampled UV offsets plus sparse pattern-image keyframes). DS material motion preserves an exact `timebaseHz`, stepped sample semantics, and per-material layer role/order, so playback does not change with renderer frame rate or rounded millisecond timing. Uniform Nitro alpha and the GLB sampler are preserved per material, including independent U/V repeat, clamp, or mirror behavior. UV-driven materials can additionally carry a world-space `uvMapping` basis, allowing independently placed 1x1 tiles to sample one continuous water/cloud/grass field. Authoring implementation: `pokemon-resort-page/tools/admin/modules/mapeditor/tile-pack-editor.js` and `tools/admin/lib/tile-pack-authoring.mjs`. Runtime loader: `pokemon-resort/src/gameplay/world3d/data/RtpksTilePackageLoader.cpp`.

sections.title: What RTPKS is for
sections.summary: Stable tile identities from PDSMS to Map Editor and bgfx.

blocks.body: Pokémon DS Map Studio tile selector: artists paint with **local tile indices** in the grid. RTPKS maps each list slot to a stable `resortTileId` that survives re-saves, appends, and handoff to Resort. The **Pokémon Resort** menu exposes Open / Save / Append RTPKS actions.
blocks.caption: PDSMS tile selector (local indices in the editor)

blocks.title: Resort tile pipeline
blocks.caption: Two files per pack (.rtpks + .rtpks.meta); owmap references the pack and paints resortTileId cells
blocks.source:
flowchart LR
    PDSMS[PDSMS tile painting] -->|Save RTPKS v2| RTPKS[.rtpks ZIP]
    PDSMS -->|sidecar| META[.rtpks.meta]
    RTPKS --> ME[Map Editor palette]
    META --> ME
    ME -->|tileLayers + tilePackage| OWM[.owmap map]
    RTPKS -->|RtpksTilePackageLoader| BGFX[OverworldBgfxRenderer]

blocks.body:
Design goals:

• **No second palette UI in PDSMS**: stable IDs live inside RTPKS; the Map Editor resolves `resortTileId` through the meta sidecar previews.
• **Native PDSMS round-trip**: `pdsms/tileset.pdsts` loads through `TilesetIO`; the editor never reconstructs tiles from runtime meshes alone.
• **Embedded runtime**: v2 packs include `runtime/manifest.json` (rpak), per-tile mesh JSON, and PNG textures so C++ and the Map Editor 3D view share one source.
• **ID preservation**: re-saving keeps existing `resortTileId` values; removed slots become `inactive` tombstones.

Empty map cells in PDSMS use local index **-1**. Resort tile ID **0 is valid**. Do not treat zero as null.

sections.title: Archive schema (v2)
sections.summary: ZIP layout, manifest, tile index, tile tabs, runtime rpak, and meta sidecar.

blocks.body: Extension: `.rtpks`. Container: **ZIP** with forward-slash paths. Reader/writer: `RtpksArchive.java`. **Version 2 only**: `RtpksManifest.VERSION = 2`; admin `inspectRtpksBuffer` and `RtpksTilePackageLoader` reject v1.

blocks.html:
Entry pathRequiredContents
manifest.jsonyesFormat id, version 2, pack metadata, paths to index files
index/tile_index.jsonyeslocalIndex → resortTileId
index/tile_tabs.jsonyesPalette tabs grouping resortTileId lists for Map Editor
pdsms/tileset.pdstsyesNative PDSMS tileset
pdsms/textures/*.pngyes*Embedded textures (*per material)
runtime/manifest.jsonyespokemon_resort.rpak: materials + tile templates
runtime/meshes/tile_{id}.jsonyes*Per-tile mesh geometry (*one per active id)
runtime/textures/*.pngyes*Runtime texture copies for C++ / editor 3D
pdsms/TilesetThumbnail.pngnoPDSMS selector thumbnail

Sibling sidecar (not inside the ZIP): {pack}.rtpks.meta: separate ZIP with pokemon_resort.rtpks.meta manifest, editor/tile_metadata.json, and editor/previews/tile_{id}.png thumbnails. Map Editor requires both files; SHA256 of the `.rtpks` must match sourceSha256 in the meta manifest.

blocks.body: Format: `pokemon_resort.tile_index`, version 1. Maps each **PDSMS local tile list index** to a stable **`resortTileId`** (uint32 in JSON). Map Editor `tileLayers` cells and the C++ renderer both reference `resortTileId`, not local index.

blocks.html:
entries[] fieldTypeDescription
localIndexnumberPosition in PDSMS tile list (0-based)
resortTileIdnumberStable Resort id (0 is valid)
keystringDiagnostic slug e.g. tile_0017
statusstringactive or inactive (tombstone)
ID assignment (TileIndexBuilder): first save allocates ids 0…n-1; re-save preserves mappings; removed tiles become inactive; appended tiles get the next unused id.

blocks.body: PDSMS **Tile tab creator** assigns tiles to named tabs (ground, trees, props, …). On save, `RtpksTileTabs.build()` writes `index/tile_tabs.json`. The Map Editor groups the RTPKS palette by these tabs.
blocks.caption: Tile tab creator in PDSMS

blocks.body: `RtpksRuntimePayloadWriter` bakes PDSMS tiles into an embedded **RPAK** document at save time. `runtime/manifest.json` uses `format: pokemon_resort.rpak`, lists materials and tile templates, and points at per-tile mesh JSON and texture PNGs under `runtime/`.

blocks.caption: C++ loader: v2 manifest + runtime meshes

blocks.body:
Written beside the pack by `RtpksEditorMetaWriter.write()`: filename pattern: `my_pack.rtpks.meta`. Contains rendered preview PNGs (one per active tile), tab assignments, footprint metadata, and a SHA256 of the source `.rtpks` so the Map Editor can detect stale sidecars.

Deploy **both** files to `pokemon-resort/assets/overworld/tilepacks/`. Upload APIs in the admin server accept `.rtpks` + `.rtpks.meta` together.

sections.title: Authoring in the Map Editor
sections.summary: Edit tabs and smart paths, import tiles, define animation, tags, and collision.

blocks.html:
Tile Pack Editor areaBehavior
TilesRename tiles, move them between palette tabs, add gameplay tags and typed properties, choose automatic collision rules, and mark a tile as a directional door with trigger-phase open and close animation semantics.
Palette tabsCreate, rename, reorder, and remove palette tabs without renumbering tile ids.
Smart pathsCreate path sets and assign connected tile variants in an editable grid.
Add tileImport one Pokemon Resort .tile bundle, textured GLB, image, or spritesheet. You can also select a batch of .tile files, preserve every bundle name and footprint, and optionally replace the chosen tab in one pack rebuild. Identical animation frames are stored once. RAE bundles carry a top-down orthographic PNG that becomes the selector and map-placement preview. The Gen 5 Map Objects panel can export every discovered animated door with source and animation metadata already attached.

blocks.body: Historical Pokémon DS Map Studio packs can still be imported. The Operations Desk preserves every existing `resortTileId`; a newly added tile receives the next unused id and deleted ids are never reused.
blocks.caption: Legacy pack import remains compatible

blocks.body: In the **Map Editor**, bind a pack and select **Edit tile pack…** below the package selector. The modal edits tab groups, smart paths, tile definitions, animation frames, gameplay tags, and collision rules. Animated tiles show a **Play animation** control in the Tiles inspector so you can verify material frames before saving. Saving refreshes the palette and 3D preview immediately.
blocks.caption: RTPKS palette in the Map Editor

blocks.body:
Typical workflow:

1. In RAE, preview a Nintendo DS BMD0 model. For a large map, open **Tile Extractor** and focus the logical material row. **Export .tile…** writes the current arrow selection. **Export all _count_…** writes every inferred straight, corner, or object occurrence to one folder with its layered GLB, exact material-motion data, UV-texture classification, and top-down orthographic preview. For Gen 5 map buildings, **Export all doors…** writes every explicit or confidently inferred door with discovery provenance and open or close clip metadata.
2. In the Map Editor, bind an RTPKS package and select **Edit tile pack…**.
3. Open **Add tile**. Choose one `.tile` file, or select the complete exported batch. Review the first bundle and select the target palette tab.
4. For a batch, choose whether to append or replace the tiles currently in that tab. Existing stable ids become inactive tombstones and are never reused.
5. Add the tile set. The editor keeps each bundle name, footprint, preview, material alpha, sampler, world-UV basis, and animation timeline, assigns new stable `resortTileId` values, and reuses identical animation textures.
6. For a door tile, enable **Door**, choose its local front, and select its open and close animation semantics. Door motion uses the trigger phase and does not run as an ambient loop.
7. For any animated tile, select **Play animation** to verify the live material motion.
8. Save the pack, paint the map, save the `.owmap`, and run the game 3D test screen to verify placement and animation.

Textured GLB, image, and spritesheet import remain available for single tiles. Older bundles without a preview are rendered top-down from their RTPKS mesh in the editor. A `.tile` bundle animates named GLB materials while leaving other materials static. Generation V water remains a UV-offset timeline; only true texture-pattern changes are stored as sparse image keyframes. World-classified UV materials add the placement anchor through their source-derived basis, so adjacent tiles do not restart the texture at every cell. The Admin viewport and bgfx runtime advance DS motion on exact stepped source ticks and keep globally synchronized layers. Trigger-phase door materials remain at the closed frame until a door script requests open or close playback. Multi-cell tiles store only an anchor in `.owmap`, but every covered cell is interactive; erasing any part clears the full footprint, and painting removes all same-layer overlaps. GLB skeletal or node clips still import at bind pose because RTPKS tile motion is material-based.

blocks.body:
Reader errors:

• Wrong `format` or unsupported manifest `version` (v1: re-export from PDSMS)
• Missing `runtime/manifest.json`, meshes, or textures
• Map Editor without `.rtpks.meta` or SHA256 mismatch after manual copy
• `editorPayload.type` not `pdsms_tileset`

sections.title: Versioning and extension
sections.summary: v1 deprecation, safe extensions, owmap glue.

blocks.body:
**v1 → v2 migration:** Re-open the tileset in PDSMS and **Save Current Tileset as RTPKS…** again. v2 adds embedded runtime meshes, `tile_tabs.json`, and the `.rtpks.meta` sidecar. Old v1-only packs cannot load in the Map Editor or C++ renderer.

**Safe extensions:** Optional manifest fields and extra ZIP entries should be ignored by readers that do not understand them. Per-tile tags can grow in `editor/tile_metadata.json` without bumping RTPKS manifest version if consumers tolerate unknown keys.

**Breaking changes:** Increment manifest `version` when JSON shape changes; update `RtpksReader`, `inspectRtpksBuffer`, and `RtpksTilePackageLoader` together. Any tool that renumbers `resortTileId` must emit an explicit remap report for painted `tileLayers` cells in existing `.owmap` files.
